fit: Positive nonlinear least squares, amplitude profiled analytically; direct intensities, including negative observations, are retained.
uncertainty: Nominal 95% profile-likelihood regions for D conditional on this model and known sigma, using the asymptotic chi-square-1 threshold: Delta SSR/sigma^2 <= chi2_1(.95). None as upper bound means unbounded. Finite-sample coverage is not validated, especially under poor identification or a boundary. The profile shape itself is the demonstrated diagnostic.
noise_design: The same fixed Gaussian noise realization is used across ramp scenarios for a controlled comparison. It is not an experimental shared-noise claim.
signal_threshold: Signal >=3sigma is only a displayed diagnostic, not a hardware limit, a universal acceptance threshold, or a D-identification criterion.
ramp_design: 24 points, gradient fractions 8..96%; b_max is set hypothetically rather than derived from any instrument calibration.

preprocessing.correction_assumption: The additive baseline is independently known in this simulation; fitting an unconstrained third parameter is not claimed to recover it reliably.
preprocessing.normalization_definition: Each attenuation point is divided by that very same integrated signal, y_i/y_i=1. A single common scaling factor for the entire series would preserve D.

limitations: Monoexponential, no exchange, convection, gradient imperfections or relaxation confounding.
One known absolute sigma and one fixed synthetic noise realization; interval widths are example-specific.
Baseline subtraction is valid here because the synthetic additive offset is independently known.
A common multiplicative normalization of the whole series preserves D; self-normalization of each point destroys attenuation.
